illusion_1_label_noise_ceiling.title: The Bayes Error / Human Label Noise Ceiling
illusion_1_label_noise_ceiling.explanation: Our system reported a 96.0% F1 headline metric. However, human intra-annotator consistency on identical queries is 46.9% (Kappa=0.0355). Any model reporting > 94% F1 on uncurated customer support is partially overfitting to human annotator noise rather than capturing a cleaner truth.

illusion_2_prevalence_shift.title: Base-Rate Prevalence Distortion (Gold Set vs In-the-Wild Stream)
illusion_2_prevalence_shift.explanation: Our gold calibration test set was stratified to 49% escalations to rigorously stress-test edge cases. In the raw Twitter stream, true Tier-0 emergencies occur in only ~1.5% of tweets. At a 1.5% base rate, a 92.3% precision on test data drops to ~65% empirical precision in production, meaning human agents will review ~1 benign false alarm for every 2 true escalations.

illusion_3_survivorship_bias.title: Public Timeline Survivorship Bias
illusion_3_survivorship_bias.explanation: The dataset only captures conversations that occurred in public view. High-value VIP passengers with dedicated phone lines, corporate contract travelers, or passengers whose tweets were deleted during high-severity PR crises are systematically under-represented in twcs.csv.
illusion_3_survivorship_bias.bound: System is calibrated on public social interactions, not full omnichannel contact center streams.
